prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your budget, the roof type and materials you want, your neighborhood, whether you have insurance/ storm damage, and the company’s reputation for workmanship and customer service. Here’s a practical way to find the best roofing company in Dallas for your roof replacement and how to choose between contenders.

How to find good candidates
- Search local reviews on Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor and Nextdoor. Look for many recent, detailed reviews (not just star counts).  
- Ask neighbors or your HOA for referrals — you can see completed jobs in your neighborhood.  
- Check for manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred Contractor, etc.). Those require training and usually mean access to better warranties.  
- Verify business registration, liability insurance and workers’ compensation (or confirmed subcontractor coverage). Ask the company to email/hand you certificates.  
- Look for a local Dallas office/phone number and a long track record in the area (not a storm-chaser).

What to ask every company (must-haves)
- Are you licensed/registered to work in Dallas (and do you obtain required permits)?  
- Can you provide proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp? (Get certificates.)  
- Do you have references from recent Dallas roof replacements? Can I see photos?  
- Are you certified by the shingle manufacturer I want? What warranties come with the materials and your workmanship?  
- What exactly is included in the written estimate (tear-off count, underlayment type, ice & water shield locations, ventilation, flashing, drip edge, number of layers removed, disposal)?  
- What is the project timeline, payment schedule, and who will supervise the work?  
- Do you provide lien releases and final inspection documentation?  
- How do you handle change orders and unexpected damage found during tear-off?

Red flags to avoid
- Pressure to sign immediately, or a “special storm” price that expires in hours.  
- No written contract or vague scope.  
- No local address or unmarked trucks, or asking for large cash-only up front.  
- Refusal to show insurance certificates or license/registration.  
- Very low bids compared to others with no explanation of lower-quality materials or omitted work.

How to compare bids (quick checklist)
- Scope clarity: Is every task and material listed?  
- Materials and brand names (shingles, underlayment, ventilation).  
- Warranty: manufacturer vs. contractor workmanship length and transferability.  
- Number of layers removed (important if you want full tear-off).  
- Permits and disposal included?  
- Timeline and start/duration.  
- Payment terms and lien release at completion.  
- References and photos of past work.

Where to vet companies in Dallas
- Google Business / Google Maps (reviews, photos)  
- Better Business Bureau (complaints history)  
- Angi/HomeAdvisor (certified pros and reviews)  
- Nextdoor and local Facebook groups for neighborhood referrals  
- City of Dallas permitting office (to confirm permits pulled on past projects)

If you’d like, I can:
- Give a short list of Dallas-area roofing companies to contact if you share your ZIP code, or  
- Help you evaluate 2–3 written estimates (you can paste them here) and point out differences and potential concerns.

Tell me your ZIP code or paste the estimates and I’ll help you next.
